summary: Iteration 5 frontend smart-handoff test on PUBLIC preview URL. The handoff JSON payload IS being written and the Studio side IS reading it (banner shows correct word count + topic + 12 B-roll prompts, default mode=Avatar for long source, handoff-switch-faceless CTA visible). HOWEVER the PRIMARY GOAL of iteration 5 — stripping bracket beat markers like [HOOK — 0:00–0:30], [SECTION N: ...], [OUTRO + CTA — ...], [INTRO BRIDGE — ...] from the avatar's script — is NOT WORKING. The script textarea on /studio still contains all 7 standalone bracket beat headers, which means the avatar would read 'HOOK zero colon zero zero to zero colon three zero' aloud — the exact failure the user complained about. Backend health not retested (frontend-only per request).

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking data-testid=handoff-switch-faceless, mode-faceless did NOT receive is-active class (mode stayed Avatar). bulk-prompts textarea never rendered as a result. Could be a flake or a state-update race; needs main agent to retest after fixing bug #1 below.

integration_issues.issue: extractNarration() in /app/frontend/src/utils/parser.js fails to strip standalone bracket beat headers when the script-engine wraps them in markdown bold (e.g. '**[HOOK — 0:00–0:30]**'). The Claude long-form output uses bold-wrapped bracket headers, so the regex /^\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*$/gm never matches because the line starts with '*', not '['. The asterisks are stripped LATER by the bold-strip regex, but by then the bracket-strip pass has already run. Result: textarea contains 7 bracket-only lines: [HOOK — 0:00–0:30], [INTRO BRIDGE — 0:30–1:00], [SECTION 1: WHY YOUR CURRENT DIET MIGHT BE FAILING YOU — 1:00–2:30], [SECTION 2/3/4 — ...], [OUTRO + CTA — 6:30–7:00]. THIS IS THE EXACT BUG ITERATION 5 WAS SUPPOSED TO FIX.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX (parser.js extractNarration): swap the order of operations OR tolerate bold-wrapping on bracket lines. Two easy fixes — (a) Move the bold/italic strip BEFORE the standalone-bracket strip so '**[HOOK ...]**' becomes '[HOOK ...]' first; (b) OR update the standalone-bracket regex to /^\s*\*{0,2}\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*\*{0,2}\s*$/gm. Verified empirically: the regex itself works correctly on a plain '[HOOK — 0:00–0:30]' line — the regex test produced clean output in-browser. The miss is the leading '**' on Claude's actual section body.
Update /app/frontend/src/utils/parser.test.cjs to include a fixture line '**[HOOK — 0:00–0:30]**\n\nContent.' so this regression can't sneak back in.

After the parser fix, retest handoff-switch-faceless click → mode-faceless is-active + bulk-prompts visible + scene-card-N rendered. If still broken, look into whether the banner re-render unmounts the button before the click registers.
critical_code_review_comments: parser.js:81 — bold-strip step runs AFTER bracket-strip step, defeating the bracket-strip on bold-wrapped headers. Reverse the order.

parser.js — the regex /^\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*$/gm uses an unbounded [^\]]* which can span newlines. Today the input lines are single-line so this is fine, but if Claude ever emits a multi-line bracket beat header, the regex will greedily eat content between brackets across paragraphs. Tighten with /^\s*\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*$/gm.

Studio.jsx — the handoff banner shows 'Switch to Faceless to use the B-roll prompts →' only when mode===AVATAR AND prompts>0. For shorts source, mode is auto-flipped to FACELESS in the SAME useEffect, so by render time mode===FACELESS and the CTA is correctly hidden. Behavior is correct — flagged for clarity only.

parser.cjs and parser.js are duplicate implementations kept in sync by hand. Consider exporting from .js only and letting the test runner use a tiny CJS shim, OR generate parser.cjs from parser.js via a build step. Duplicate-source bugs are inevitable otherwise.

Studio.jsx handoff useEffect — the 10s auto-dismiss timer is set inside the useEffect but its cleanup return is OUTSIDE the try/catch try block path; if the JSON parse throws, the cleanup still runs against a possibly-uninitialized handoffBannerTimer.current (which is fine because it's a ref initialized to null). Defensive but not a bug.

rca_of_the_issue: extractNarration() steps execute in this order: (1) strip inline B-ROLL/ON-SCREEN directive cues, (2) strip standalone bracket-only lines /^\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*$/gm, (3) strip markdown bold **...**, (4) strip italic *...*, (5) collapse whitespace. Claude's long-form output emits section beat headers as '**[HOOK — 0:00–0:30]**' (asterisks BEFORE the opening bracket). Step 2's regex anchors to '^\s*\[' so a line starting with '*' is not matched. Step 3 strips the asterisks, but by then we're past step 2 and the bracket line survives the rest of the pipeline. Fix: swap step 2 and step 3, OR widen step 2's regex to ^\s*\*{0,2}\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*\*{0,2}\s*$. Empirically verified in-browser — the regex works on a plain bracket line but does not work on a **-wrapped bracket line.
